workflow_runs.name: PR
workflow_runs.display_title: fix(workspace): a refusing --install must not roll the stored guard back (KEE-958)

head_commit.message:
fix(workspace): a reverting guard lane must not roll the stored guard back

The refusal-path fix in 1f14cdd6e orders the two guard CONTENTS by asking
whether the newest commit carrying this lane's content is an ancestor of the
newest commit carrying the stored content. That is sound for a linear behind
lane. It is wrong for a revert.

  c1 OLD -> c2 NEW -> c3 REVERT-to-OLD, fleet parked on c2, operator on c3

The newest carrier of OLD is the REVERT, a DESCENDANT of c2, so ancestry
answered false, the code read that as "this lane is ahead", and published the
OLD bytes over the NEW ones -- fleet-wide, on a run that also exited 1 saying
it had refreshed the guard. Measured on KEE-960: stored 9a015171 -> 0ed9476f.
The suite was 25/25 green on it, because a linear fixture cannot produce that
ordering.

Two questions, two different answers, and conflating them is what shipped:

  (1) has this lane's content EVER been in force at or before the stored
      guard's newest carrier?  answered by ANY carrier. In the shape above c1
      is an ancestor of c2, so OLD is recognised as superseded and left alone.
  (2) failing that, is this lane genuinely ahead?  answered by the NEWEST
      carrier, which is the commit the lane stands on. This keeps the KEE-955
      benefit -- a lane carrying a genuinely newer guard still fixes the fleet
      on a refusing run.

(1) is checked first and it wins; it is the only rule that catches a revert.
guardRevision() becomes guardCarrierIndex(), a blob->commits map built in one
pass rather than a git log plus a rev-parse chain per content. A dropped
"unknown" return on a genuine git failure is restored, so a failed merge-base
is still reported as ordering-not-established instead of a confident decision.

The AHEAD test in 1f14cdd6e was a FALSE TEST, and that is why the revert bug
was green. It seeded content A, committed B = A + comment, then committed A
again as "current" -- so the lane's guard was the superseded A while HEAD was
newer. That is a revert shape, byte-for-byte the state the new test builds,
with the opposite assertion, and it passed by way of the defect this commit
removes. It now builds the genuine advance (content never in force before)
and asserts the shape it built, so a green run cannot again be a fixture that
never produced the case.

Verified: 26/26 in this suite, from a 23/23 baseline before any of it. The
REVERT test fails against 7d4360f84 and against 1f14cdd6e, and passes here.
The "never refresh on refusal" retreat is caught by the NEWER test and by the
pre-existing refusal test. Sibling suites: check-worktree-isolation 17/17,
e2e-shard 11/11, run-vitest-stable-shard 24/24. End to end on the real guard
revisions 1023ffe31 (9a015171) and 83669412d (0ed9476f), all three shapes:
behind and revert no longer downgrade, and the novel guard still reaches the
fleet.

Not tested: macOS, Windows path handling of git hash-object --stdin,
concurrent installers, a repository where the guard was never committed, a
non-linear merged guard history, and CI on either PR.

workflow_runs.name: Storybook Visual
workflow_runs.display_title: fix(issues): stop a refused or stale run binding from stranding an issue (TES-91)

head_commit.message:
fix(issues): charge a run's own task as its own source, not the lowest id

Greptile P1 on #14107. resolveRunCheckoutSourceIssueId ordered the
run's bound issues by id and took the first, so a run bound to several
issues was charged the cross-issue budget for writes to some of its own
tasks and not others, decided by UUID order.

The ordering has a real job: with no unique constraint on checkout_run_id
or execution_run_id, a run can hold several, and the pick must be stable
so the same run and board produce the same sourceIssueId on every write.
It is only a tie-break. It is not an answer to which of the run's issues
is its own, and the function already receives targetIssueId without
using it.

So: when the run is bound to the issue being written, that issue is the
source, and the write is not counted. This is the rule the caller already
states, and the rule the file's own comment states. Otherwise fall
through to the ordered pick, unchanged, so a foreign write is still
attributed to a stable source.

Test pins the id sort order explicitly rather than trusting randomUUID,
so it fails against the ordered pick for the reason under test. Negative
control: reverting the fix fails only the new test, 1 failed / 7 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Paperclip Agent <agent@paperclipai.local>
